div.head: II Cn 13.2
div.ab: And lochwa þone flyman fede oððe feormie, gylde V pund þam cingce, butan he hine geladige, þæt he hine fleame nyste.
And lochwa þone flyman fede oððe feormige, gylde fif pund þam cyningce, buton he hine geladige, þæt he hine fleame nyste.
Qui forsbannitum pauerit uel ei firmationem aliquam exhibuerit, emendet regi V libras, nisi se adlegiet, quod infugatum eum nesciebat.
⁊ lóchwá ðone fleman féde oððe feormie, gylde fif pund ðam cýnge, butan he hine geladige þæt he hine flema nyste.
And lochwa þone flyman fede oððe feormie, gylde V pund þam cingce, butan he hine geladige, þæt he hine fleame nyste.
And whoever feeds or harbours the fugitive shall pay £5 to the king, unless he clear himself by a declaration that he did not know that he was a fugitive.
And anyone who feeds or shelters a fugitive must pay five pounds to the king, unless he can exonerate himself by proving that he did not know he was a fugitive.
And whoever feeds or harbours the fugitive is to pay five pounds to the king, unless he clear himself, that he did not know him to be a fugitive.
Und wer immer jenen Geächteten nährt oder herbergt, zahle dem König 5 Pfund, es sei denn, er erweise sich rein, dass er ihn nicht in Verbannung gewusst habe.
And whoever feeds or harbours that outlaw, let him pay the king 5 pounds, unless he clears himself [by showing] that he did not know him to be outlawed.
div.note: B's ‘flema’ (as ‘outlaw’) — Liebermann suggests B may mean the instrumental of ‘fle(a)m’ (outlawry). Liebermann compares II As 20.8.
